claim: The Ctf19 complex (Ctf19c) in yeast and the constitutive centromere associated network (CCAN) in other organisms creates the foundation of a kinetochore.
source: A group of proteins called the Ctf19 complex (Ctf19c) in yeast and the constitutive centromere associated network (CCAN) in other organisms creates the foundation of a kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about kinetochore organization.

claim: The Ctf19c/CCAN influences the timing of kinetochore assembly.
source: The Ctf19c/CCAN influences the timing of kinetochore assembly, sets its location by associating with a specialized nucleosome containing the histone H3 variant Cse4/CENP-A, and determines the organization of the microtubule attachment apparatus.
evidence: This is stated as a known function of the Ctf19c/CCAN in the abstract.

claim: The Ctf19c/CCAN sets kinetochore location by associating with a specialized nucleosome containing the histone H3 variant Cse4/CENP-A.
source: The Ctf19c/CCAN influences the timing of kinetochore assembly, sets its location by associating with a specialized nucleosome containing the histone H3 variant Cse4/CENP-A, and determines the organization of the microtubule attachment apparatus.
evidence: This is stated as a known function of the Ctf19c/CCAN in the abstract.

claim: The Ctf19c/CCAN determines the organization of the microtubule attachment apparatus.
source: The Ctf19c/CCAN influences the timing of kinetochore assembly, sets its location by associating with a specialized nucleosome containing the histone H3 variant Cse4/CENP-A, and determines the organization of the microtubule attachment apparatus.
evidence: This is stated as a known function of the Ctf19c/CCAN in the abstract.

claim: The structure of a reconstituted 13-subunit Ctf19c was determined by cryo-electron microscopy at ~4 Å resolution.
source: We present here the structure of a reconstituted 13-subunit Ctf19c determined by cryo-electron microscopy at ~4 Å resolution.
evidence: This is the primary experimental finding reported in the abstract.

claim: The structure accounts for known and inferred contacts with the Cse4 nucleosome.
source: The structure accounts for known and inferred contacts with the Cse4 nucleosome and for an observed assembly hierarchy.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the structural determination in the abstract.

claim: The structure accounts for an observed assembly hierarchy.
source: The structure accounts for known and inferred contacts with the Cse4 nucleosome and for an observed assembly hierarchy.
evidence: This is stated as a result of the structural determination in the abstract.

claim: During cell division, depolymerizing microtubules pull copies of the genome into developing daughter cells.
source: During cell division, depolymerizing microtubules pull copies of the genome into developing daughter cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about cell division in the introduction.

claim: The pulling force is transmitted to the centromere through the kinetochore.
source: The pulling force is transmitted to the centromere through the kinetochore, the apparatus that determines the position of the microtubule contact point along the chromosome, couples chromosome movements to microtubule dynamics, organizes and responds to the activities of kinases, and establishes a chromosomal domain that promotes proper microtubule attachment (Biggins, 2013; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018; McKinley and Cheeseman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The kinetochore determines the position of the microtubule contact point along the chromosome.
source: The pulling force is transmitted to the centromere through the kinetochore, the apparatus that determines the position of the microtubule contact point along the chromosome, couples chromosome movements to microtubule dynamics, organizes and responds to the activities of kinases, and establishes a chromosomal domain that promotes proper microtubule attachment (Biggins, 2013; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018; McKinley and Cheeseman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The kinetochore couples chromosome movements to microtubule dynamics.
source: The pulling force is transmitted to the centromere through the kinetochore, the apparatus that determines the position of the microtubule contact point along the chromosome, couples chromosome movements to microtubule dynamics, organizes and responds to the activities of kinases, and establishes a chromosomal domain that promotes proper microtubule attachment (Biggins, 2013; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018; McKinley and Cheeseman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The kinetochore organizes and responds to the activities of kinases.
source: The pulling force is transmitted to the centromere through the kinetochore, the apparatus that determines the position of the microtubule contact point along the chromosome, couples chromosome movements to microtubule dynamics, organizes and responds to the activities of kinases, and establishes a chromosomal domain that promotes proper microtubule attachment (Biggins, 2013; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018; McKinley and Cheeseman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The kinetochore establishes a chromosomal domain that promotes proper microtubule attachment.
source: The pulling force is transmitted to the centromere through the kinetochore, the apparatus that determines the position of the microtubule contact point along the chromosome, couples chromosome movements to microtubule dynamics, organizes and responds to the activities of kinases, and establishes a chromosomal domain that promotes proper microtubule attachment (Biggins, 2013; Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018; McKinley and Cheeseman, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The kinetochore is an assembly of biochemically distinct subcomplexes.
source: The kinetochore is an assembly of biochemically distinct subcomplexes (Cheeseman et al., 2002; De Wulf et al., 2003), and coordinated appearance and disappearance of these subcomplexes over evolutionary timescales suggests a functional modularity (van Hooff et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Coordinated appearance and disappearance of kinetochore subcomplexes over evolutionary timescales suggests a functional modularity.
source: The kinetochore is an assembly of biochemically distinct subcomplexes (Cheeseman et al., 2002; De Wulf et al., 2003), and coordinated appearance and disappearance of these subcomplexes over evolutionary timescales suggests a functional modularity (van Hooff et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from evolutionary observations with supporting citation.

claim: The Ctf19c/CCAN anchors the kinetochore on chromosomal DNA.
source: One such assembly is the Ctf19c/CCAN, which anchors the kinetochore on chromosomal DNA.
evidence: This is stated as a known function of the Ctf19c/CCAN.

claim: Kinetochore proteins assemble on specialized nucleosomes in which Cse4/CENP-A replaces histone H3.
source: Kinetochore proteins assemble on specialized nucleosomes in which Cse4/CENP-A replaces histone H3.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about kinetochore assembly.

claim: In animals, at least two conserved kinetochore proteins, CENP-C and CENP-N, confer specificity for CENP-A.
source: In animals, at least two conserved kinetochore proteins, CENP-C and CENP-N, confer specificity for CENP-A (Carroll et al., 2010; Carroll et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The vertebrate CCAN stabilizes CENP-A nucleosomes so that they are maintained throughout the cell cycle and during extended periods of cellular quiescence.
source: The vertebrate CCAN also stabilizes CENP-A nucleosomes so that they are maintained throughout the cell cycle and during extended periods of cellular quiescence (Cao et al., 2018; Guo et al., 2017; Smoak et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The protein domains of CENP-C and CENP-N that confer CENP-A selectivity are present in yeast Mif2 and Chl4, respectively.
source: The protein domains of CENP-C and CENP-N that confer CENP-A selectivity are present in yeast Mif2 and Chl4, respectively, indicating that the mechanism of CENP-A/Cse4 nucleosome recognition is probably conserved.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about protein domain conservation.

claim: The mechanism of CENP-A/Cse4 nucleosome recognition is probably conserved.
source: The protein domains of CENP-C and CENP-N that confer CENP-A selectivity are present in yeast Mif2 and Chl4, respectively, indicating that the mechanism of CENP-A/Cse4 nucleosome recognition is probably conserved.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on domain conservation.

claim: Ctf19c proteins couple cohesin recruitment with DNA replication initiation.
source: In addition to recognizing Cse4 and supporting outer kinetochore assembly, Ctf19c proteins couple cohesin recruitment with DNA replication initiation and direct successful meiotic chromosome segregation (Hinshaw et al., 2017; Marston et al., 2004; Vincenten et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Ctf19c proteins direct successful meiotic chromosome segregation.
source: In addition to recognizing Cse4 and supporting outer kinetochore assembly, Ctf19c proteins couple cohesin recruitment with DNA replication initiation and direct successful meiotic chromosome segregation (Hinshaw et al., 2017; Marston et al., 2004; Vincenten et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Yeast Ctf19c proteins co-purify from cells.
source: The yeast proteins, like their human orthologs, co-purify from cells and depend on each other for kinetochore localization (Cheeseman et al., 2002; De Wulf et al., 2003; Foltz et al., 2006; Klare et al., 2015; Okada et al., 2006; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Yeast Ctf19c proteins depend on each other for kinetochore localization.
source: The yeast proteins, like their human orthologs, co-purify from cells and depend on each other for kinetochore localization (Cheeseman et al., 2002; De Wulf et al., 2003; Foltz et al., 2006; Klare et al., 2015; Okada et al., 2006; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016; Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: There are 13 Ctf19c subunits.
source: There are 13 Ctf19c subunits (Figure 1A, Table 1, Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016), and these associate with a second complex containing Mif2/CENP-C and the Cse4/CENP-A nucleosome.
evidence: This is stated in the text and shown in Figure 1A and Table 1, with a supporting citation.

claim: Ctf19c subunits associate with a second complex containing Mif2/CENP-C and the Cse4/CENP-A nucleosome.
source: There are 13 Ctf19c subunits (Figure 1A, Table 1, Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016), and these associate with a second complex containing Mif2/CENP-C and the Cse4/CENP-A nucleosome.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Two copies of each Ctf19c subunit probably decorate each nucleosome core particle.
source: Two copies of each Ctf19c subunit probably decorate each nucleosome core particle (Weir et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a probable stoichiometry with a supporting citation.

claim: Human CCAN proteins have connectivity and assembly properties similar to those of the yeast Ctf19c proteins.
source: Human CCAN proteins have connectivity and assembly properties similar to those of the yeast Ctf19c proteins (Table 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the text and supported by Table 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nearly all human CCAN proteins are required for mitosis.
source: Unlike their S. cerevisiae counterparts, however, nearly all human CCAN proteins are required for mitosis, while all but two (Okp1 and Ame1) are dispensable in yeast (see Table S1 in Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: All but two yeast Ctf19c proteins (Okp1 and Ame1) are dispensable in yeast.
source: Unlike their S. cerevisiae counterparts, however, nearly all human CCAN proteins are required for mitosis, while all but two (Okp1 and Ame1) are dispensable in yeast (see Table S1 in Hinshaw and Harrison, 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Conservation of sequence and domain arrangement for the common components suggests considerable architectural similarity between yeast and human complexes.
source: Although this difference might imply divergent organizations in yeast and humans, conservation of sequence and domain arrangement for the common components suggests considerable architectural similarity.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on sequence conservation.

claim: The Ctf19c was assembled from individual parts (Ame1-Okp1, Ctf19-Mcm21, Nkp1-Nkp2, Chl4-Iml3, Ctf3-Mcm16-Mcm22, and Cnn1-Wip1).
source: We assembled the Ctf19c from individual parts (Ame1-Okp1, Ctf19-Mcm21, Nkp1-Nkp2, Chl4-Iml3, Ctf3-Mcm16-Mcm22, and Cnn1-Wip1; Figure 1A–B) and purified the recombinant complex to homogeneity by size exclusion chromatography (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in this study, shown in figures.

claim: The recombinant Ctf19c complex was purified to homogeneity by size exclusion chromatography.
source: We assembled the Ctf19c from individual parts (Ame1-Okp1, Ctf19-Mcm21, Nkp1-Nkp2, Chl4-Iml3, Ctf3-Mcm16-Mcm22, and Cnn1-Wip1; Figure 1A–B) and purified the recombinant complex to homogeneity by size exclusion chromatography (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A–B).
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in this study, shown in figures.

claim: Molecular weight determination indicated the presence of two copies of each subunit.
source: Molecular weight determination indicated the presence of two copies of each subunit (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Cryo-EM images of the Ctf19c prepared by crosslinking gradient sedimentation showed monodisperse particles.
source: Cryo-EM images of the Ctf19c prepared by crosslinking gradient sedimentation showed monodisperse particles (Figure 1D), and two-dimensional class averages matched those calculated for an uncrosslinked sample (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Two-dimensional class averages of crosslinked samples matched those calculated for an uncrosslinked sample.
source: Cryo-EM images of the Ctf19c prepared by crosslinking gradient sedimentation showed monodisperse particles (Figure 1D), and two-dimensional class averages matched those calculated for an uncrosslinked sample (Figure 2A, Figure 1—figure supplement 2C–D, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation shown in multiple figures.

claim: Several class averages resembled projections of a low-resolution tomographic reconstruction of the yeast inner kinetochore.
source: Several class averages resembled projections of a low-resolution tomographic reconstruction of the yeast inner kinetochore (McIntosh et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an observation comparing the current data to a previous study.

claim: A twofold symmetry axis in the calculated density map related equivalent sides, which were separated by a central cavity.
source: A twofold symmetry axis in the calculated density map related equivalent sides, which were separated by a central cavity (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM density map shown in Figure 2B.

claim: An extended helical network, which matches secondary structure predictions for Ame1, Okp1, and Nkp1/2, spans the bottom of the map.
source: An extended helical network, which matches secondary structure predictions for Ame1, Okp1, and Nkp1/2, spans the bottom of the map.
evidence: This is an observation from the density map combined with secondary structure predictions.

claim: A cluster of five short alpha helices constitute a domain that reaches into the central cavity, and this density matched a crystal structure of the N-terminal domain of CENP-N.
source: A cluster of five short alpha helices constitute a domain that reaches into the central cavity, and this density matched a crystal structure of the N-terminal domain of CENP-N (Pentakota et al., 2017), the human ortholog of Chl4.
evidence: This describes fitting of a known crystal structure into the cryo-EM density.

claim: A crystal structure of Chl4374-450-Iml3 from budding yeast fit into the remaining beta sheet density.
source: A crystal structure of Chl4374-450-Iml3 from budding yeast (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013) fit into the remaining beta sheet density.
evidence: This describes fitting of a known crystal structure into the cryo-EM density.

claim: The helical array in the top part of the map corresponds to the Ctf3 complex (Ctf3c), which contains the Ctf3, Mcm16, and Mcm22 proteins.
source: The helical array in the top part of the map corresponds to the Ctf3 complex (Ctf3c), which contains the Ctf3, Mcm16, and Mcm22 proteins.
evidence: This is an assignment of density in the cryo-EM map to specific proteins.

claim: Mcm16 and Mcm22 associate as a coiled-coil that traverses the predicted HEAT repeats in Ctf3.
source: Mcm16 and Mcm22 associate as a coiled-coil that traverses the predicted HEAT repeats in Ctf3 (Basilico et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an observation from the structure with a supporting citation.

claim: Cnn1-Wip1, which form a heterodimeric histone fold complex, were visible at the tip of the Ctf3 helical array.
source: Cnn1-Wip1, which form a heterodimeric histone fold complex, were visible at the tip of the Ctf3 helical array.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM density map.

claim: From bottom to top, the organization of the Ctf19c matches published recruitment dependencies for Ctf19c proteins.
source: From bottom to top, this organization matches published recruitment dependencies for Ctf19c proteins (Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016); subcomplexes at the bottom of the map are required for recruitment of their partners towards the top.
evidence: This is an observation comparing the structure to published biochemical data.

claim: Subcomplexes at the bottom of the map are required for recruitment of their partners towards the top.
source: From bottom to top, this organization matches published recruitment dependencies for Ctf19c proteins (Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016); subcomplexes at the bottom of the map are required for recruitment of their partners towards the top.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: A refined map corresponding to a single Ctf19c protomer showed amino acid side chain density for much of the complex.
source: A refined map corresponding to a single Ctf19c protomer (see Materials and methods) showed amino acid side chain density for much of the complex, guiding modeling of individual polypeptide chains and their interactions (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the refined cryo-EM map.

claim: The Ctf19c/CCAN is a defined complex in which subunits interdigitate rather than a network of binary interactions.
source: The structure shows that, rather than a network of binary interactions, the Ctf19c/CCAN is a defined complex in which subunits interdigitate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural data.

claim: Several subunits project N-terminal extensions that are disordered in the reconstruction and that support regulated interactions with other kinetochore components.
source: Several subunits project N-terminal extensions that are disordered in our reconstruction and that support regulated interactions with other kinetochore components.
evidence: This is an observation from the structure combined with known functional information.

claim: The conserved four-protein COMA complex connects inner and outer kinetochore proteins.
source: The conserved four-protein COMA complex connects inner and outer kinetochore proteins.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about COMA function.

claim: The Ame1 and Okp1 subunits interact with DNA, Mif2, and Chl4.
source: Published work shows that the Ame1 and Okp1 subunits interact with DNA, Mif2, and Chl4, although precise contacts have been difficult to define (Hornung et al., 2014; Schmitzberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: An N-terminal extension of the Ame1 protein recruits outer kinetochore proteins by making an essential contact with the MIND complex.
source: An N-terminal extension of the Ame1 protein recruits outer kinetochore proteins by making an essential contact with the MIND complex (Hornung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Ctf19 and Mcm21 have regulatory functions and recruit Ctf19c components downstream of Ame1-Okp1.
source: Ctf19 and Mcm21 have regulatory functions and recruit Ctf19c components downstream of Ame1-Okp1 (Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The Nkp1/2 heterodimer stabilizes COMA.
source: The Nkp1/2 heterodimer stabilizes COMA (Schmitzberger et al., 2017), but neither protein is needed for viability or to recruit other Ctf19c members to the complex (Cheeseman et al., 2002; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Neither Nkp1 nor Nkp2 is needed for viability or to recruit other Ctf19c members to the complex.
source: The Nkp1/2 heterodimer stabilizes COMA (Schmitzberger et al., 2017), but neither protein is needed for viability or to recruit other Ctf19c members to the complex (Cheeseman et al., 2002; Pekgöz Altunkaya et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The organization of Ame1-Okp1 and Nkp1/2 resembles that of the MIND complex.
source: The organization of Ame1-Okp1 and Nkp1/2, which interact in pairs near their N termini and all four together near their C termini, resembles that of the MIND complex (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Dimitrova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an observation from the structure compared to a known structure with a supporting citation.

claim: Ame1-Okp1 and Nkp1/2 interact in pairs near their N termini and all four together near their C termini.
source: The organization of Ame1-Okp1 and Nkp1/2, which interact in pairs near their N termini and all four together near their C termini, resembles that of the MIND complex (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Dimitrova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the structure.

claim: Two N-terminal four-helix bundles, comprising helical hairpins of Ame1 and Okp1 and Nkp1 and Nkp2, are distinct but adjacent 'head' domains.
source: Two N-terminal four-helix bundles, comprising helical hairpins of Ame1 and Okp1 (analogous to head II of MIND) and Nkp1 and Nkp2 (analogous to head I), are distinct but adjacent 'head' domains.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the structure.

claim: Intermediate segments of Okp1, Ame1, and Nkp1 contact the C-terminal RWD domains of the Ctf19-Mcm21 heterodimer.
source: Intermediate segments of Okp1, Ame1, and Nkp1 contact the C-terminal RWD domains of the Ctf19-Mcm21 heterodimer.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the structure.

claim: C-terminal parts of Okp1 Ame1, Nkp1 and Nkp2 form a parallel, four-chain, helical coil.
source: C-terminal parts of Okp1 Ame1, Nkp1 and Nkp2 form a parallel, four-chain, helical coil.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the structure.

claim: The crystal structure of Ctf19-Mcm21 bound to a fragment of Okp1 helped define the sequence register and orientation of Okp1 early in map interpretation.
source: The crystal structure of Ctf19-Mcm21 bound to a fragment of Okp1 helped define the sequence register and orientation of Okp1 early in map interpretation (Schmitzberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes how a previous structure aided in interpreting the current cryo-EM map.

claim: Published hydrogen-deuterium exchange experiments confirmed chain identities for the extended helices.
source: Published hydrogen-deuterium exchange experiments confirmed chain identities for the extended helices (Schmitzberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This cites published data that supports the structural assignments.

claim: Positions of chemical crosslinks allowed assignment of much of the corresponding peptide sequence.
source: Positions of chemical crosslinks allowed assignment of much of the corresponding peptide sequence (Hornung et al., 2014).
evidence: This cites published data that supports the structural assignments.

claim: Unchanged hydrogen-deuterium exchange within the Mcm21 C-terminal RWD domain in the presence or absence of Ame1-Okp1 corroborated the assignment to Nkp1 of density that snakes across the Mcm21 RWD surface.
source: Unchanged hydrogen-deuterium exchange within the Mcm21 C-terminal RWD domain in the presence or absence of Ame1-Okp1 (Schmitzberger et al., 2017) corroborated the assignment to Nkp1 of density that snakes across the Mcm21 RWD surface.
evidence: This uses published data to support a structural assignment in the current model.

claim: Connections between the Ctf19-Mcm21 C-terminal RWD domains and Ame1-Okp1 recall previously-described RWD interactions.
source: Connections between the Ctf19-Mcm21 C-terminal RWD domains, which are recurring structural modules in the kinetochore (Schmitzberger and Harrison, 2012), and Ame1-Okp1 recall previously-described RWD interactions (Corbett and Harrison, 2012; Petrovic et al., 2014; Schmitzberger et al., 2017).
evidence: This compares the observed structure to previously described structures with supporting citations.

claim: Ctf19 and Mcm21 have N-terminal extensions that are flexible in the absence of other components.
source: Ctf19 and Mcm21 have N-terminal extensions that are flexible in the absence of other components (Schmitzberger and Harrison, 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Density for parts of the N-terminal extensions of Ctf19 and Mcm21 connects the ordered parts of Ctf19-Mcm21 to the Ctf3c.
source: We now see density for parts of these segments that connect the ordered parts of Ctf19-Mcm21 to the Ctf3c (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the current cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Protein sequence alignments predict that the N-terminal extension of Mcm21 has a conserved helix at its tip.
source: Protein sequence alignments predict that the N-terminal extension of Mcm21 has a conserved helix at its tip (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is a prediction from sequence analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2A.

claim: Deletion of the Mcm21 N-terminal extension (mcm21-Δ95) produced defective Ctf3 localization.
source: To test the idea that this fragment engages the Ctf3c and influences its recruitment to the kinetochore, we imaged cells expressing Ctf3-GFP as they progressed through the cell cycle (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B, Figure 3—figure supplement 3). Deletion of the Mcm21 N-terminal extension (mcm21-Δ95) produced defective Ctf3 localization, an effect that was similar in magnitude to that produced by CTF19 deletion.
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation from live-cell imaging shown in Figure 3C and supplements.

claim: The effect of mcm21-Δ95 on Ctf3 localization was similar in magnitude to that produced by CTF19 deletion.
source: Deletion of the Mcm21 N-terminal extension (mcm21-Δ95) produced defective Ctf3 localization, an effect that was similar in magnitude to that produced by CTF19 deletion.
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation from live-cell imaging.

claim: In both ctf19Δ and mcm21-Δ95 cells, residual Ctf3 localization was observed.
source: In both ctf19Δ and mcm21-Δ95 cells, we observed residual Ctf3 localization, a phenotype also observed in chl4Δ cells (Pot et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation with a supporting citation.

claim: Residual Ctf3 localization is a phenotype also observed in chl4Δ cells.
source: In both ctf19Δ and mcm21-Δ95 cells, we observed residual Ctf3 localization, a phenotype also observed in chl4Δ cells (Pot et al., 2003).
evidence: This cites a previous observation with a supporting citation.

claim: Ctf19-Mcm21 recruits the Ctf3c through Mcm21N.
source: We infer that Ctf19-Mcm21 recruits the Ctf3c through Mcm21N and that additional interactions with either COMA or Cse4-Mif2 support partial Ctf3 localization in the absence of Ctf19-Mcm21.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: Additional interactions with either COMA or Cse4-Mif2 support partial Ctf3 localization in the absence of Ctf19-Mcm21.
source: We infer that Ctf19-Mcm21 recruits the Ctf3c through Mcm21N and that additional interactions with either COMA or Cse4-Mif2 support partial Ctf3 localization in the absence of Ctf19-Mcm21.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observations.

claim: The Chl4-Iml3 complex is heterodimeric with two functional domains.
source: The Chl4-Iml3 complex is heterodimeric with two functional domains (Hinshaw and Harrison, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The Chl4 N-terminal domain binds DNA.
source: The Chl4 N-terminal domain binds DNA, while the Chl4 C-terminal domain associates with Iml3 to make an extended beta sheet that recruits other Ctf19c components to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Chl4 function.

claim: The Chl4 C-terminal domain associates with Iml3 to make an extended beta sheet that recruits other Ctf19c components to the kinetochore.
source: The Chl4 N-terminal domain binds DNA, while the Chl4 C-terminal domain associates with Iml3 to make an extended beta sheet that recruits other Ctf19c components to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about Chl4 function.

claim: Vertebrate CENP-A recognition by CENP-N/L depends on contact between the CENP-N β3-β4 loop and the CENP-A RG loop.
source: Vertebrate CENP-A recognition by CENP-N/L depends on contact between the CENP-N β3-β4 loop and the CENP-A RG loop (Chittori et al., 2018; Pentakota et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: An N-terminal bundle of five alpha helices in CENP-N forms a pyrin domain.
source: An N-terminal bundle of five alpha helices, which forms a pyrin domain (Pentakota et al., 2017), contributes to the DNA binding activity of the protein.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: The N-terminal pyrin domain of CENP-N contributes to the DNA binding activity of the protein.
source: An N-terminal bundle of five alpha helices, which forms a pyrin domain (Pentakota et al., 2017), contributes to the DNA binding activity of the protein.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Yeast Chl4 shares structural features with CENP-N including the pyrin domain.
source: Our density map showed that yeast Chl4 shares these structural features (Figure 4A) and also enabled modeling of the Chl4 linker domain, which connects the two previously-described functional modules and provides extensive contacts between Chl4 and Ctf19-Mcm21 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the cryo-EM structure shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The Chl4 linker domain connects the two previously-described functional modules and provides extensive contacts between Chl4 and Ctf19-Mcm21.
source: Our density map showed that yeast Chl4 shares these structural features (Figure 4A) and also enabled modeling of the Chl4 linker domain, which connects the two previously-described functional modules and provides extensive contacts between Chl4 and Ctf19-Mcm21 (Figure 4B).
